summary: Not as an oversold signal. Buying while MFI(14) was below 20, or as it crossed back up through 20, did the same as random entries on 1h, 4h and daily. The result that holds up runs the other way: after MFI(14) went above 80, price kept rising, and shorting it did 10.5% worse than random after 20 days on daily.

verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. On 1h in uptrends it did worse than random.

notes: Buying while MFI(14) was below 20 on 1h gave 6,778 entries in 1,392 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.07% behind random entries, inside the luck band. The cross back up through 20 enters about a third as often and lands in the same place. On 4h and daily, both settings were also the same as random.

The oversold result splits by trend on 1h. While the pair was above its 200-day SMA, entries below 20 did 0.29% worse than random. That shows at 10, 20 and 50 candles and holds without its strongest stretch. In downtrends it was the same as random. The cross up through 20 in uptrends also looked worse, but only because of signals on Dec 18–19, 2024.

Shorting while MFI(14) was above 80 on daily did 10.5% worse than random after 20 days. It holds without its strongest stretch, between Aug 10 and Sep 12, 2021, and shows at 10 candles too. At 50 and 100 candles it was the same as random. On 1h the pooled result sits just inside the band, but in uptrends the short did 0.42% worse than random at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. In downtrends it showed nothing.

On 4h, shorting above 80 did 1.01% worse than random, but only because of the run between Aug 27 and Sep 7, 2021. The cross down through 80 looked worse on 4h and daily for the same reason: its gap rests on signals on Aug 27–31, 2021 on 4h, mostly on SOL. Without that stretch, both were the same as random.

The cross up through 50 and the cross down through 70 were the same as random on all three timeframes. In downtrends the cross up through 50 beat random by 0.34% on 4h and 2.89% on daily. Each rests on one stretch, May 4–7, 2025 on 4h and between Dec 21, 2022 and Jan 2, 2023 on daily, so neither holds.

For a long DCA bot, MFI(14) below 20 adds no timing on these pairs, and on 1h in uptrends it picked worse entries than random. Leave it out, or let the DCA orders and take profit do the work. Where MFI carries information is above 80: it marked buying that continued, mostly while the pair was above its 200-day SMA. A short bot that opens on that reading trades against the trend, so it is better used as a condition that holds short entries back.
